A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same INFER research work. All 16 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original INFER classification experiments, cross-architecture evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, cross-architecture evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The UFC construction, additive integration with natural instances, optimization objective, static-label generation, and MixUp procedure remain identical in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same classification tasks on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K. No dataset, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership within each setting. The reported comparisons involving Random, DC, KIP, RFAD, MTT, SRe2L, and G-VBSM are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Tables 5–7 retain the same evaluation architectures, IPC budgets, metrics, preprocessing, augmentation, batch sizes, and training schedules. No experimental protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The UFC and architecture-ensemble ablations, feature-duplication analysis, decision-boundary visualizations, sample-difficulty comparison, and label-divergence analysis are retained unchanged in Section 4.3 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: The result tables retain the same ± uncertainty reporting. Neither version supplies different run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings are unchanged, including Appendix D. For example, Table 2 reports the same INFER ImageNet-1K accuracy of 62.5±0.2 for ResNet-50 at IPC 50 and the same 4.04% compression ratio.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, compression-ratio definition, and Equations 1–5 retain identical mathematical content. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about overcoming class-specific distillation barriers, improving budget efficiency, capturing inter-class features, and reducing soft-label storage.

C2.justification: The interpretations of feature duplication, decision boundaries, and static-label compatibility remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning datasets exceeding 1,000 classes and the separate treatment of intra-class and inter-class features.

D1.justification: The hardware disclosure, implementation information, Algorithms 1–2, and training recipes in Appendix C are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 60 references and the same research positioning appear in Section 2 and Appendix B. No cited work or substantive comparison with prior research changes.

P1.justification: v2 merges the abstract's two paragraphs into one while preserving its wording and updates the arXiv version/date text. Section order, terminology, and the substantive narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract reformatting shifts Figure 1 and reflows text across pages 1–3. Table 8 loses an extra horizontal rule beneath its top border, slightly tightening its layout. Figure content, captions, and table entries remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the method, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information throughout the paper and appendices. The abstract reformatting, opening-page reflow, and Table 8 border adjustment are cosmetic and produce no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
